## 1. Fit each modality separately

CHORALE transforms each assay on an appropriate measurement scale and runs independent component
analysis (ICA) without phenotype or covariates. Covariate weighting therefore cannot change factor
extraction. Several ICA starts are aligned, and CHORALE keeps the stable run closest to the other
runs (the medoid). Stability is reported.

## 2. Estimate adjusted effects

For every factor, one multivariable model includes phenotype and every eligible covariate shared by
all modalities. This gives the phenotype effect after adjustment for the other included variables.

Continuous covariates are standardised. Binary covariates contribute one contrast. A categorical
covariate with several levels contributes a block of contrasts. Each secondary block has equal total
weight, so a variable does not become influential merely because it has many levels. Standard errors
and coefficient covariance matrices are retained, so imprecise effects provide less evidence.

Phenotype must be present in every modality, must have compatible levels, and must include the
declared reference level (`control` by default). Covariates that are absent, incompatible, too
incomplete, or not jointly estimable are reported with a reason.

## 3. Let phenotype define the candidates

The primary affinity compares adjusted phenotype effects only. A simultaneous spectral assignment
uses all modality pairs at once, producing a cycle-consistent proposal.

Bootstrap resampling repeats the phenotype comparison. An alternative is removed only when its
phenotype loss is reproducibly worse than the best loss. Alternatives that cannot be separated on
phenotype remain in the candidate set.

## 4. Let secondary covariates refine, never rescue

Every other eligible shared covariate is compared only inside the phenotype candidate set. These
covariates can confirm the phenotype assignment or choose among phenotype-equivalent candidates.
They cannot promote a candidate excluded by phenotype and cannot turn absent phenotype support into
a resolved result.

There is deliberately no numerical parameter such as “60% phenotype”. Priority comes from the
sequence of decisions, not an arbitrary weighted average.

## 5. Calibrate the search

A joint phenotype permutation null keeps ICA fixed and repeats matching and modality-subset
selection. Each permutation records the largest statistic reached anywhere in the search. Reported
p-values therefore use max-statistic family-wise error control across searched factors and subsets.

Pathway analysis is separate evidence. It uses score-residual permutations relative to the fixed
assay, then recalculates loadings by matrix regression. This preserves feature correlation and
feature annotations. Design and pathway evidence are related because both use fitted factors; they
are not described as independent.

## 6. State what the unpaired design cannot identify

Matching factors does not reconstruct measurements that would have been observed in the same
individual. CHORALE reports bounds on compatible cross-modal correlations, not a point estimate.
Resampling refits each resampled container, aligns re-estimated factors, and reports a sensitivity
envelope around the bound endpoints.
